data.why: the app generates all Monte Carlo scenario data at runtime via numpy.random.default_rng(seed); there is no file-based input to supply

goals: run the 200-scenario Monte Carlo Monte Carlo simulation (seed=2025) and confirm zero false permits across non-compliant and attack scenarios
inspect the ASI-PLC latency distribution for valid-credential welds and verify it stays within the 500 ms permissive window
vary scenario counts and random seed to test whether the Compliance Bit decision logic remains fail-locked under different mixes of MitM, replay, and timeout faults
examine the PLC state distribution (IDLE/COMPLIANT/NON_COMPLIANT/SOFT_LOCK/HARD_LOCK) and scenario detail table to trace individual decision cycles
export the full state-count JSON summary for comparison against the paper's Table 8 results

review.summary: The tree describes the app accurately: it reproduces the seed-2025 Table 8 run, stress-tests fail-lock behaviour across seeds and attack mixes, and traces single decisions through a smart workaround for the 30-row table. The sampled screens back every claim. It needs small fixes before filing: drop the widget-level JSON phase, correct the input step sizes, and say plainly that the False permits and Soft lock cards don't count timeout outcomes the way the labels suggest.
